summary: Shoshone County, ID: an L-4 cab on a pole tower (dated 1931 or 1934); the cab moved to Spyglass Peak in 1943 or 1944 and the tower is gone.

facts.status_note: Tower gone per the state index; the L-4 cab was moved to Spyglass Peak

events.note: Pole tower with L-4 cab. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1934 instead.
L-4 cab moved from McDonald Peak to Spyglass Peak for living quarters. Willhite gives 1944.

Spyglass ground house, which Willhite ties to the moved cab, renovated and put on the rental program (Idaho Fire Lookouts dates the renovation to 2019). Recreation.gov says restoration began in 2012 and finished in 2019.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts site and firelookout.com date the pole tower with L-4 cab to 1931; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1934. No source settles it, so the story reports both.
Idaho Fire Lookouts, the Forest Lookouts site, firelookout.com and the NHLR give 1943 for the cab move; Willhite gives 1944. The story uses 1943 and notes Willhite's date.

Recreation.gov calls the Spyglass ground house a 1930s building; Willhite ties it to the L-4 cab moved from McDonald Peak in 1943 or 1944; Idaho Fire Lookouts lists that move without naming the ground house. Both descriptions are in the story.

notes_for_editor: Gone tower: the site today is undocumented in every source read; the story says so. The 1931 vs 1934 build date and the 1943 vs 1944 cab move are unresolved. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history for this lookout, so staffing is left out. No fires found. Access to the McDonald Peak site is unknown and left out of facts. The brief's design L-4 and agency Coeur d'Alene National Forest are confirmed. The Spyglass cab is the moved structure; the story covers both sites as the brief's moved-tower rule requires. Recreation.gov's 1930s date for the ground house conflicts with the 1943/1944 move; flagged, not resolved.
